newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Illovo to reopen Mozambique sugar mill.
newsitem.headline: Illovo to reopen Mozambique sugar mill.

text.p: South African producer Illovo Sugar Ltd is to invest $18.5 million in Mozambique's mothballed Maragra sugar mill, which should start crushing cane again in 1998, a spokesman said on Thursday.
Maragra, which closed 12 years ago, has 6,200 hectares of surrounding sugar land, suggesting potential annual sugar production of 57,000 tonnes.
At present only 100 ha is planted to cane.

Illovo is to take a 50 percent stake in Maragra Sugar for $9 million and will contribute half of a the $19 million needed to rehabilitate the plant and surrounding infrastructure. The company expects to raise funds to pay for the project through offshore borrowings.

The Durban-based firm will have the management contract for both the operation and overhaul of the mill. Its partners in the venture are a Portuguese family business, Mozambique banks and the Mozambique government.
Agricultural rehabilitaition will reuqire a further $25 million, to be funded by other investors and a group of South African farmers who plan to lease surrounding sugar land.
Illovo also said it was negotiating with the Kenyan government to obtain an equity stake in a Kenyan mill it was rehabilitating.
Earlier this year it signed a 21 million rand deal to remove bottlenecks at the South Nyanza Sugar Company mill near Lake Victoria. The mill, opened in 1980, is one of seven operating in Kenya.
Illovo hopes to lift production capacity to more than 78,000 tonnes of sugar a year from 69,000 at present.
